page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed around a balanced compute-to-memory configuration. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores of an Intel x86_64 processor with two threads per core, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 256 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. It does not include local storage or bundled hardware GPUs, requiring persistent disk storage options for stateful operations.

Hardware architecture highlights include modern instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8). Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile results across parallelized computing workloads, including Geekbench multi-core execution (17690.0), PassMark CPU score (67610.19), software compilation via Clang (41502.0), and encryption processing (57650.04). Large-block memory throughput reaches 277.75 GB/sec for uncached reads and 122.41 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain within median levels, registering 1777.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1689.08 in stress-ng single-core tests.

The presence of AMX instructions enables high throughput for CPU-based machine learning inference, recording 229.23 tokens per second for prompt processing and 33.98 tokens per second for text generation on medium 7B models. In transactional environments, the system demonstrated 70.46 million Redis SET operations per second and 86.82 GB/sec static web throughput. Given the absence of local storage and discrete GPUs, this instance provides cost-efficient multi-threaded compute density suited for large-scale web serving, microservices clusters, enterprise database servers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven batch inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical Intel cores, 256 GB of RAM, and 260 MB of L3 cache. Maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance contains no local disk storage or bundled discrete GPUs. The underlying Intel architecture features AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, yielding top-quartile performance in multi-core metrics, software compilation, database operations, and CPU-based LLM inference. Memory throughput is also strong, delivering 277.75 GB/sec on uncached reads. Single-core processing aligns with median performance ranges across standard benchmarks. The configuration offers balanced compute density for horizontally scaled web services, CI/CD build environments, Redis caching layers, and in-memory database deployments.
